paragraphs: Rav Dimi of Nehardea: Menachot 35a; Chullin 15b; Pesachim 110b; Bava Batra 138b. At the end of Yevamot, 121a, at Bei Hedya they brought up a drowned man after three days, and Rav Dimi permitted his wife to marry. “When there is a wound, water causes it to swell …” is not Rav Dimi’s statement, and I do not know why he wrote it. He brought merchandise: Bava Batra 22; see Rav Adda bar Ahavah for the matter at length. “When Rav Dimi went up”—this is difficult, for Nehardea is in Babylonia, yet it uses the language of ascent. Perhaps it is because it is on the frontier, as stated in chapter Mi Shehotziuhu, or according to Taanit 10a, that Nehardea is above Sura (see above, Shmuel). Amemar said in the name of Rav Dimi of Nehardea. Mar Zutra replied to Amemar: Chullin 51b. He ruled that the law follows Rav Huna. See part 1: Rav Dimi reigned in year 4140, for three years; I do not know which Rav Dimi.
